question: Which daemon-wide process, concurrency, time, action, artifact, upload, download, and quarantine ceilings bound the first supervised browser vertical?
selected_option: Keep the first browser vertical immediate and tightly supervised: one browser instance, one isolated context, four pages, one in-flight action, 768 MiB browser-tree RSS, 2.5-second launch-ready p95, 15-minute session lifetime, 100 actions, 128 MiB captured artifacts, 512 MiB quarantine, 256 MiB per download, and 64 MiB per upload on the selected Linux reference host.
rationale: The user explicitly selected OPT-BROWSER-BUDGET-LEAN-CONTROLLED. Sequential execution inside one isolated context preserves the strongest first-vertical supervision and reconciliation boundary while still allowing a four-page investigation without adopting parallel browser effects or multi-context resource growth.

required_semantics: the daemon owns one Playwright supervisor and one supervised browser process tree; no client, agent, remote gateway or WebAssembly component can connect to or launch another browser endpoint
the first vertical admits one non-persistent isolated browser context with at most four pages and exactly one in-flight action across the context

the effective resource allowance is the fail-closed intersection of these daemon-wide ceilings, the live browser-context grant, the exact action envelope and current policy; a grant can narrow but never enlarge a ceiling
browser-tree RSS includes the Playwright supervisor, browser parent, renderer, GPU, utility, network and other descendant processes attributable to the supervised instance

launch ready begins at supervisor-approved browser-process creation and ends only after the pinned browser reports ready, the isolated context exists, a blank page completes the versioned supervisor handshake and the daemon accepts its identity

launch-ready p95 is evaluated over at least 30 independently recorded samples on the selected native Ubuntu 24.04 x86-64 reference environment with raw samples and exact Playwright, JavaScript-runtime, browser-build and launch-argument identities
session lifetime and action count are hard upper bounds; expiry or exhaustion blocks new actions and initiates bounded evidence finalization and context teardown
captured-artifact bytes include decoded traces, screenshots, DOM or accessibility snapshots, console records, bounded request and response evidence and other retained observations before compression
quarantine bytes include all unreleased downloaded content and derived scan artifacts; each download and upload is also checked against its per-item decoded-byte ceiling before transfer proceeds

an attempted page, context, instance, action, memory, lifetime, artifact, quarantine, download or upload expansion beyond a ceiling is refused or terminated with an explicit bounded outcome and redacted evidence

resource termination during an observation yields failed or cancelled; termination after dispatch of a potentially effectful action yields uncertain, blocks dependent actions and cannot trigger an implicit retry
orphan cleanup, graceful shutdown, forced termination and quarantine retention remain bounded even when the browser or supervisor crashes or stops responding
budget counters and outcomes are daemon-owned and cannot be reset by navigation, redirect, popup, page replacement, context recreation, reconnect, token refresh or client restart
non_implications: these ceilings do not grant an origin, navigation, credential, file, permission, action, download, upload, raw-CDP operation or external effect
selecting a budget does not satisfy the pending Essays security-owner or Work Owner browser-effect-policy gate
the ceilings are unproven conformance targets and do not show that Playwright or the pinned browser currently meets them
this decision does not select exact Playwright, JavaScript-runtime, browser-build, sandbox, process-accounting, quarantine, scanner, artifact or benchmark implementations
meeting the resource ceilings does not prove browser safety, semantic correctness, external-effect success, security, support, release or production readiness
this decision does not authorize dependency installation, browser launch, navigation, credential use, file transfer, publication, release, deployment or external effects

owner_gate.required_owner: Essays Project owner plus Essays security owner plus Work Owner effect-policy owner
owner_gate.effect_until_satisfied: Playwright installation, browser launch, grant issuance, navigation, credential use, file transfer and browser effects prohibited

remaining_blockers: Essays security-owner and Work Owner review of the Playwright driver, scoped browser-grant policy and selected resource ceilings
exact pinned Playwright, JavaScript runtime, browser build, launch arguments, sandbox and supervisor protocol identities
exact Linux descendant-process accounting, memory enforcement, cancellation, teardown and orphan-cleanup binding
artifact accounting, redaction, quarantine, scan, retention, release and secure-deletion schemas
native benchmark and independent conformance evidence for launch, memory, lifetime, action, artifact and file ceilings
Product Capability decision and dependent contracts
authored ontology closure and DomainSpec generation
deferred_decisions: Multiple contexts, concurrent observation actions, longer sessions, larger artifacts and larger file transfers require a separately reviewed browser-budget decision and renewed security and conformance evidence.
The exact enforcement mechanism may use Linux-native process grouping or another verified binding, but it cannot weaken descendant coverage or fail-closed outcomes.
